question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Ganga but flows directly into the Bay of Bengal? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Ghaghara
Kosi
Gomti
Mahanadi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahanadi

Explanation:
Mahanadi is not a tributary of the Ganga; it is an independent river that flows directly into the Bay of Bengal. It originates in the Sihawa hills of Chhattisgarh and passes through Odisha. Major tributaries of the Ganga include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Kosi, Gomti, Gandak, and Son. Ghaghara originates in Nepal and joins the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh. Kosi, known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar', is a left-bank tributary. Gomti meets the Ganga in Varanasi. Mahanadi is known for the Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world. It is also called the 'Ruhr of India' due to its rich mineral deposits in the basin.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Source of Mahanadi → Sihawa hills, Chhattisgarh
☛ Major dam on Mahanadi → Hirakud Dam
☛ Longest tributary of Ganga → Yamuna
☛ Right bank tributaries of Ganga → Yamuna, Son, Gandak
☛ Left bank tributaries of Ganga → Ghaghara, Kosi, Gomti
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी नदी गंगा की सहायक नदी नहीं है, बल्कि बंगाल की खाड़ी में सीधे मिलती है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: घाघरा
कोसी
गोमती
महानदी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है महानदी

Explanation:
महानदी गंगा की सहायक नदी नहीं है, बल्कि यह एक स्वतंत्र नदी है जो सीधे बंगाल की खाड़ी में गिरती है। यह छत्तीसगढ़ और ओडिशा राज्यों से होकर बहती है। गंगा की प्रमुख सहायक नदियों में यमुना, घाघरा, कोसी, गोमती, गंडक, सोन आदि शामिल हैं। घाघरा नेपाल में उत्पन्न होकर गंगा में मिलती है, कोसी बिहार में गंगा की सहायक है, और गोमती उत्तर प्रदेश में गंगा में मिलती है। महानदी का उद्गम छत्तीसगढ़ के सिहावा पहाड़ियों से होता है और यह हीराकुंड बांध के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।

question: Which of the following lakes in Rajasthan is artificial?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Ramgarh
Ana Sagar
Pushkar
Sambhar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ana Sagar

Explanation:
Most lakes in Rajasthan are natural, but Ana Sagar is an artificial lake. It was built in the 12th century by Anaji Chauhan, the ruler of Ajmer, by damming the Luni River. In contrast, Ramgarh lake is also artificial, but among the given options, Ana Sagar is the correct answer. Pushkar and Sambhar are natural lakes. Pushkar Lake is considered sacred, and Sambhar Lake is India's largest saline water lake. Ana Sagar Lake is a famous tourist spot, with marble pavilions and temples along its banks.

☛ Largest natural lake in Rajasthan → Sambhar Lake

पुष्कर
सांभर

Explanation:
राजस्थान की अधिकांश झीलें प्राकृतिक हैं, लेकिन आना सागर एक कृत्रिम झील है। इसका निर्माण 12वीं शताब्दी में अजमेर के शासक अनाजी चौहान द्वारा करवाया गया था। यह झील बांध बनाकर लूनी नदी के पानी को रोकने से बनी है। दूसरी ओर, रामगढ़ झील भी कृत्रिम है, लेकिन प्रश्न में दिए गए विकल्पों में से केवल आना सागर सही है। पुष्कर और सांभर प्राकृतिक झीलें हैं। पुष्कर झील पवित्र मानी जाती है और सांभर झील भारत की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की झील है। आना सागर झील पर्यटन स्थल के रूप में प्रसिद्ध है और इसके किनारे संगमरमर की छतरियां और मंदिर स्थित हैं।

question: Which group of islands lies between 8° – 12° 13″ North latitude and 71° – 74° East longitude? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Lakshadweep
Rameswaram
Nicobar
Andaman
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lakshadweep

Explanation:
Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory of India, located in the Arabian Sea between 8°–12°13' North latitude and 71°–74° East longitude. It consists of 36 islands, of which 11 are inhabited. Its capital is Kavaratti. This group of islands is made of coral reefs and shares a maritime border with the Maldives. Minicoy is the southernmost island. The name Lakshadweep means 'one lakh islands'. The main language is Malayalam, and the tribal language is Mahal. It is famous for tourism and rich in biodiversity.

question: Which of the following states is NOT covered by the Ganga Plain? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Punjab
Haryana
West Bengal
Bihar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
The Ganga Plain is primarily spread across northern India, including Haryana, West Bengal, and Bihar. The state of Punjab is not part of the Ganga Plain; it lies in the Indus River system plain. The Ganga Plain is formed by rivers originating from the Himalayas, such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi. This plain extends from Uttarakhand through Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal. In Punjab, rivers like Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum, which are tributaries of the Indus, flow, separate from the Ganga system. Thus, Punjab is not covered by the Ganga Plain.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा राज्य गंगा के मैदान से आच्छादित नहीं है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: What is the dominant soil type in the Great Plains of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Laterite soil
Black cotton soil
Alluvial soil
Red soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial soil

Explanation:
The dominant soil type in the Great Plains of India is Alluvial soil. This soil is formed by sediments deposited by rivers and is mainly found in the northern plains of the Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra river valleys. Alluvial soil is of two types: new (Khadar) and old (Bhangar). It is rich in potash but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus. This soil covers about 40% of the country's area and is highly fertile for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses. Among other options, laterite soil is found in high-temperature regions, black cotton soil in the Deccan Plateau, and red soil in southern India.

☛ Deficiencies in Alluvial soil → Nitrogen and phosphorus
☛ Main river valley for Alluvial soil → Ganga valley
☛ Coverage of Alluvial soil in India → About 40%
☛ Nutrient rich in Alluvial soil → Potash
question_hi: भारत के विशाल मैदानों में प्रमुख मृदा प्रकार क्या है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: लैटेराइट मृदा
काली कपास मृदा
जलोढ़ मृदा
लाल मृदा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जलोढ़ मृदा

Explanation:
भारत के विशाल मैदानों में प्रमुख मृदा प्रकार जलोढ़ मृदा है। यह मृदा नदियों द्वारा लाए गए अवसादों से बनी है और मुख्यतः उत्तरी भारत के मैदानी क्षेत्रों जैसे गंगा, सिंधु और ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी घाटियों में पाई जाती है। जलोढ़ मृदा नई (खादर) और पुरानी (बांगर) दो प्रकार की होती है। यह पोटाश में समृद्ध लेकिन नाइट्रोजन और फास्फोरस में कम होती है। यह मृदा देश के लगभग 40% क्षेत्र में फैली हुई है और गेहूं, चावल, गन्ना, दालें जैसी फसलों के लिए उपजाऊ है। अन्य विकल्पों में, लैटेराइट मृदा उच्च तापमान वाले क्षेत्रों में पाई जाती है, काली कपास मृदा दक्कन के पठार पर, और लाल मृदा दक्षिणी भारत में मिलती है।

question: Which of the following physical factors influences the compactness of rural settlements in dry regions like Rajasthan? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Groundwater salinity
Availability of water
Soil fertility
Altitude
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Availability of water

Explanation:
In dry regions like Rajasthan, the compactness of rural settlements is primarily influenced by the availability of water. Due to limited water sources, people tend to settle around water bodies such as wells or ponds, leading to nucleated settlements. Low rainfall and scarce groundwater force communities to cluster together for easy access to water. Other factors like groundwater salinity affect water quality but do not directly determine settlement compactness. Soil fertility is important for agriculture, but in arid areas, water availability takes precedence. Altitude may relate to water availability in hilly regions, but Rajasthan's plains make it less significant. Thus, water availability is the key physical factor influencing the compactness of rural settlements in dry regions.

question: How many national waterways have been declared for development under the National Waterways Act, 2016? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: 122
111
100
150
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 111

Explanation:
Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, a total of 111 national waterways have been declared for development. This act subsumed the previously declared 5 national waterways and added new ones, aiming to promote inland water transport in the country and reduce pressure on road and rail networks. question: India’s dependency on food aid reduced after the Green Revolution. Which US program had earlier provided wheat aid to India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: The Indo-Afghanistan border is officially referred to as _______. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Line of Control
McMahon Line
Durand Line
Radcliffe Line
solution:

Explanation:
The India-Afghanistan border is officially known as the Durand Line. This boundary was established in 1893 by British officer Sir Mortimer Durand between British India and Afghanistan. The Durand Line is approximately 2,640 km long and passes through Pakistan's Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces.

question: Which of the following Indian states are situated on the Bangladesh border? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Sikkim, Nagaland, Meghalaya, West Bengal, Mizoram
Mizoram, Tripura, Sikkim, Manipur, West Bengal
West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
West Bengal, Assam, Sikkim, Nagaland, Meghalaya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram

Explanation:
The Indian states sharing a border with Bangladesh are West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. West Bengal has the longest border with Bangladesh. Assam borders Bangladesh in the northern part. Meghalaya touches Bangladesh in the central region, while Tripura is surrounded on three sides by Bangladesh. Mizoram shares a border in the southeast. Sikkim, Nagaland, and Manipur do not border Bangladesh; Sikkim is bordered by China, Bhutan, and Nepal; Nagaland by Myanmar and Assam; and Manipur by Myanmar. The total length of the India-Bangladesh border is about 4,096 km, with West Bengal having the largest share. These states are important for trade and cultural ties with Bangladesh.

question: Which is the most available and most intensively used soil for agriculture in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (15/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Alluvial soil
Red Soil
Desert Soil
black soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial soil

Explanation:
The most available and most intensively used soil for agriculture in India is Alluvial soil. This soil is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers and is extensively found in the northern plains. It is rich in potash and lime but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus. This soil is highly fertile for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and maize. Alluvial soil is classified into Khadar (new alluvium) and Bhangar (old alluvium). It covers about 40% of India's total land area and fulfills the major portion of the country's food grain requirement.

☛ What percentage of India's area is covered by Alluvial soil? → About 40%

साल्टोरो कांगरी शिखर भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच नियंत्रण रेखा (LoC) के पास स्थित है। यह साल्टोरो पर्वतमाला का हिस्सा है जो काराकोरम रेंज में आता है। यह शिखर समुद्र तल से लगभग 7,742 मीटर ऊंचा है और सियाचिन ग्लेशियर के निकट स्थित है। यह क्षेत्र भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमा विवाद का हिस्सा रहा है और दोनों देशों की सेनाओं द्वारा नियंत्रित किया जाता है। साल्टोरो कांगरी की भौगोलिक स्थिति इसे सीमा सुरक्षा के दृष्टिकोण से महत्वपूर्ण बनाती है।
